bug_semantics: When a plugin lacked READ_FILES, PluginSandbox attempted to confine filesystem access by replacing only builtins.open with restricted_open. pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes and io.open retained independent file-opening paths, and pathlib/io were available to plugin code, so an untrusted plugin could read or modify paths outside the sandbox's allowed directories without passing _is_safe_path.
flaw_origin: Commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef created the plugin sandbox and first implemented _restrict_file_operations as a single-name monkey patch: it assigned builtins.open = restricted_open but did not interpose io.open or pathlib.Path methods. The same commit advertised a zero-trust security sandbox, made this incomplete hook the READ_FILES enforcement boundary, and therefore originated the bypass rather than merely moving or refactoring existing vulnerable code.
ai_marker: BIC commit object author and committer are Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>; its message contains the exact markers '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-mcjj-qw7m-j3cp identifies openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py, demonstrates Path('/etc/passwd').read_text(), states the affected range as <1.4.0, and names d0be3e9 as the fix. In the validated clone, `git log d0be3e9^ -L 479,512:openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` follows the vulnerable function through formatting and policy changes to 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef, whose added lines 217-251 call _restrict_file_operations when READ_FILES is absent and replace only builtins.open. Independent `git log --all -S'builtins.open = restricted_open' -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` and `-S'def _restrict_file_operations'` each return only 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef. `git diff --name-status 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` reports `A`, directly proving the entire vulnerable file and mechanism are absent from the immediate parent tree. `git cat-file -p 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef` proves the one-parent topology, human author/committer, Claude Code generation line, and Claude co-author trailer. `git show d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f` shows the direct repair: save and replace io.open plus pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes/unlink/mkdir/rmdir, route each through the sandbox path check, and restore every original method afterward. Its immediate parent e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092 had added pathlib and io to shared blocked-module constants as precursor hardening, while d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f is the advisory-named commit that directly interposes the bypassing APIs. `git tag --contains` places the BIC first in v1.3.0 (and all v1.3.x tags) but not v1.2.1, and places the fix first in v1.4.0 and later tags, matching the patched boundary.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle begins with the normal, one-parent feature commit 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef: its parent has no plugin_sandbox.py, and it introduces both the claimed READ_FILES boundary and the incomplete builtins.open-only enforcement. pathlib.Path uses pathlib/io entry points rather than the replaced builtins name, so the advisory's Path and io proof of concept bypasses the exact mechanism written by that commit. Later commits 642fb2bdec8af6f1d592c322dfa98647e145fcef and 35499f201ae2dc531d1194f6810c953d8b9af78b changed restoration and allowed-path policy while retaining that same single-hook design; ccb60e1a29ef67700128ca54eb25a95413d71ff1 only reformatted the relevant line. Thus blame is only a lead, while the -L history, two -S origin searches, and direct parent-tree addition establish 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef as the smallest real BIC, not a move, revert, backport, merge, or squash carrier. The first release containing it is v1.3.0; the advisory's direct atomic fix d0be3e989b1632eadb68e17d07294cbf9ac57c1f is first contained by v1.4.0, so the repository history refines the practical vulnerable interval to the v1.3.x releases within the advisory's broader <1.4.0 range.
